title: A spectrum shows behaviour, not a culprit's mugshot
summary: Frequency energy, throttle dependence, eRPM harmonics, filter positions, and downstream signals are complementary clues—not interchangeable verdicts.

blocks.caption: What each Spectrum mode contributes
rows: A peak alone rarely identifies its mechanical cause.
Does a ridge move as throttle changes?
Throttle is only a proxy for motor speed.
Does energy track measured motor harmonics?
Requires eRPM data and the correct motor pole count.

blocks.title: Filters answer different parts of the problem

blocks.caption: Filter roles in the evidence
rows: Tracks per-motor harmonics derived from recorded eRPM.
Alignment needs usable eRPM and the correct motor pole count.
Tracks remaining spectral peaks not already handled by the motor-harmonic path.
Following a peak does not identify the physical part that created it.
Attenuate a broader high-frequency region in the gyro or D-term path.
Attenuation and added delay must be judged together.

blocks.text: Configured filter overlays show where recorded settings act. Comparing unfiltered gyro, filtered gyro, D term, and motor output can show what remains downstream. Every filter attenuates something and adds delay, so 'more filtering' is not a strategy; it is merely a direction.

blocks.title: Reference guides are heuristic
blocks.text: Prop-size bands and familiar dB references are context, not universal safety limits. Craft stiffness, mass, props, motor speed, sampling, windowing, and normalization all change the picture. Measured eRPM bands and the actual recorded filter configuration are stronger evidence when available.
